analysis.title: A fragile AI rebound
key_insights: Equities decoupled to the upside from a rates selloff after a hot October CPI print, driven by AI catalysts (CoreWeave results, Anthropic's IPO, OpenAI revenues). MSCI World is up about 3% this week, erasing last week's drawdown.
Sentiment soured this morning on reports that Nvidia's board is considering replacing J. Huang. Nvidia fell as much as 10% in after-hours trading.
Hawkish macro backdrop is a headwind for equities. A 25bp Fed hike is fully priced for December, with a non-trivial chance of a half-point move. Natixis's base case remains a 25bp hike.
October core CPI was +0.3% MoM against +0.2% expected, the third consecutive monthly beat. The US 2Y yield rose 17 bps and the 10Y rose 11.4 bps to 5%.

Bunds and Gilts followed Treasuries lower: German 10Y +5.2 bps to 3.32%, UK 10Y +9.3 bps to 5.22%. UK Q3 preliminary GDP of +0.7% QoQ (fastest in two and a half years) reinforces expectations that the Bank of England keeps hiking.
Equity moves: Nikkei +4.2%, Euro Stoxx 50 +1.6%, S&P 500 +1.1%, MSCI EM +1.6% on Asian chipmakers. Hang Seng was the laggard at -0.5%.

Nvidia leadership turmoil weighs on AI and tech stocks in Asia. Alibaba fell as much as 7% on fears of tighter US scrutiny. AMD, Broadcom and Alphabet gained after hours on bets they could win business from Nvidia.

CoreWeave Q3-26: revenue $3.7bn (+168% YoY) vs $3.6bn consensus, backlog $132.5bn, EPS -$1.27 vs -$1.46 expected. FY-26 revenue guidance raised to $13.0-13.3bn from $12-13bn. FY-26 capex is $37-39bn and Q4-26 interest expense is projected at $1.05-1.15bn. The stock gained about 25%.

CoreWeave funding: weighted average cost of debt fell 250 bps sequentially to 7.9%, a DDTL facility is upcoming, and management ruled out unsecured debt at current yields. It expects $9bn of client prepayments next quarter and caps 2027 parent-level capital raises at $5bn.
Credit: iTraxx Main tightened 1.5 bps and X-Over 8 bps. CoreWeave's euro 8.5% 2032 bond rose 4.7 price points and its USD bonds 1-2 points. Oracle 5Y CDS tightened 2.5 bps and Broadcom's 1 bp.

FX: DXY rose 1.2% to 102.90, the highest since May 2025. EUR/USD fell 1.0% to 1.1093, GBP/USD fell 1.1% to 1.3275, and USD/JPY broke above 159.86. EM currencies weakened, with IDR near record lows and BRL at a 15-month low.
Natixis remains cautious on IDR and Indonesia after the VP's resignation, citing policy risk premium, MSCI index-exclusion warnings and continued passive outflows.
Gold fell 2.7% on the stronger dollar and rising real yields.
South Korea's first 10-day exports rose 112% YoY on chips and unemployment fell to 2.5%. Consumption is subdued, giving the BOK room to stay on hold.

Siemens raised its 2027 revenue growth outlook to +11% from +9%, citing industrial AI and data centers. Digital Industries growth is above the 8% consensus, and Q4 2026 order backlog is implied at nearly EUR35bn vs EUR28bn expected.

tension_points.theme: AI equity rebound vs hawkish Fed
tension_points.bull_case: AI catalysts (CoreWeave's results, Anthropic's IPO, OpenAI revenues) lifted equities despite the rates selloff, with the MSCI World up about 3% on the week.
tension_points.bear_case: A hawkish macro backdrop with a fully priced 25bp December hike and a chance of 50bp, plus Nvidia leadership turmoil, is a headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A half-point Fed hike at the December 9 meeting, or data and financial conditions that push the Fed toward a more aggressive path.
